    The last row sits below the reference and is the only one that is not an honest accounting of a logarithm: it prices relations among unknown base logarithms, which determine logP(Q) not at all. Every other row is a correction to this ledger’s own arithmetic — four made the attack look better, the fifth made it look worse by 22.65 and came from an external review agent. None is a fact about the curve. Current optimum: 2 Frobenius orbits (B = 262), 12-point relations split 11+1, quotiented table, 1,011 EB charged at zero. The structure is run end to end on small curves and recovers a planted logarithm in 6 of 6 cells (amortised_attack.json).

    Parity is below the floor, so it is unreachable rather than unreached. Balancing the build against the streamed side collapses every configuration to total = 2√(K₁ · U · C(n,s) · r) with K₁ = 0.265358. U ≥ 2 (one orbit, plus d) and C(n,s) ≥ n ≥ 2, so every configuration costs at least 265.54 whatever the support size, relation length, split or table layout. The reference is 260.81: parity sits 2-4.73 below the floor, and closing it would need the constant to fall 26.6× with nothing left to take it from. Structurally, the 262 automorphisms enter rho’s constant inside its square root, while the Frobenius quotient divides index calculus’s unknown count and table size — both real, worth 214 together, and neither touching the square root a two-list collision search over a space of size r must pay. Moving it needs a decomposition oracle cheaper than that square root, not a better constant.

    Decomposing the points is not the hard part; finding the decomposition is. At the challenge parameters a target of ECC2K-130 does have factor-base decompositions — the yield law C(|F|, m)/#E holds to within 1.09× over twelve toy cells (one small-base outlier at 0.57× aside), it needs only dim V ≥ 45 at m = 3, the cofactor-4 class admits every m ≥ 2 measured on the curve itself, and certified m = 2, 3, 4 witnesses with S4 = 0 are in the artefact. Finding one is what costs: relations × targets × oracle = m · 2131 independently of the factor-base dimension, so the best implicit-base variant is 2132.58, 2+71.77× rho, and no table rescues it — at 230 through 270 entries rho is cheaper than the best decomposition cell while storing nothing. (This sentence also said plain BSGS on the same memory beat every cell; that part is withdrawn by the second accounting correction below.) Stated as a demand on the oracle: it would have to beat exhaustive search over its own candidate set by 270.19 + log₂ m, a number that does not move with m or with l because it is the product law (experiments/ecc2k130_point_decomposition.json).

    A trace-zero factor base yields twice, and that is worth exactly one bit. A base whose abscissae lie in ker Tr sits inside 2E, an index-2 subgroup, so every sum of its points stays there — and the target subgroup is inside it too. The sums are spread over #E/2, not #E, so a target is hit twice as often as C(|F|, m)/#E says. Measured exhaustively over every target of the order-r subgroup at n = 13, 17, 19: the generic base occupies 0.98–1.00 × #E and the trace-zero base 0.49–0.50 × #E, a yield factor of 1.97–2.04. The product law reads m · 2n−1 for such a base, still flat in the dimension; the table above prices a generic subspace and would move from 2132.58 to 2131.58. One bit against a gap of seventy-two; class engineering (experiments/ecc2k130_point_decomposition.json).

    Accounting correction: the Frobenius collapse does not need a subspace. The classification that leaves only dimensions 0, 1, 130, 131 at n = 131 classifies invariant subspaces; GGMP's collapse asks only for π(F) = F, and since 131 is prime every abscissa outside F2 has an orbit of exactly 131, so a union of orbits is Frobenius-stable at any size. The product law becomes m · 2n/n and the bottom of the family moves from 2132.58 to 2124.99, 2+64.18× rho — paid for by materialising the base (244.5 points at m = 3, 223.4 at m = 6), because an orbit union has no low-degree membership polynomial. What 131 being prime forbids is having the collapse and the implicit base, not the collapse itself. Seven bits against a gap of sixty-four; class accounting, not a gain (experiments/ecc2k130_decomposition_targets.json).

    Second accounting correction: the tabulated rows never took the collapse. The collapse needs only a materialised base, and every tabulated row materialises one, yet the pair-table, triple-table and memory-capped rows were priced without it — and cost_cell’s collapse path never folded the subset-sum table. It surfaced as a disagreement: the IC tournament’s measured crossover for this family on Koblitz orbit bases (0.831, 1.396, 2.207 × rho at n23a1, n37a0, n43a1; against the tournament worker’s rho, which the triple-counted control found unmatched) carried to r = 2129 sat about 211 below the pair-table row. With both folds the m = 2 row moves from 2+28.55 to 2+20.76× rho (m = 3: 2+29.77 to 2+21.82), within 1.7 bits of the tournament’s family model (2+19.07) and inside its measured rate band carried out 97 bits (2+8.4 to 2+19.4, an extrapolation from three cells). The optimum needs a 280-entry folded table. Capped at 230–270 entries the corrected cells now beat BSGS as that comparison priced it (max(M, r/M), no automorphisms), so that claim is withdrawn; rho still beats every corrected cell at every budget, by 24 at 270 entries and 235 at 230. The implicit-base product law and the required-speed-up invariant are untouched. Class accounting, not a gain (experiments/ecc2k130_tabulated_collapse.json).

    Deciding is localising, for any detector that takes its target as input. A hypothetical decomposition oracle that answers only yes/no for the whole factor base looks far weaker than one that hands over the summands. It is not. Let R decompose; for each candidate P in the base draw a base point Q of the same cofactor class and ask the detector about R − P + Q — a class match keeps the query inside the target subgroup, so even a subgroup-only detector suffices. If P is a summand the query point is literally an m-sum of base points and the answer is yes by construction; if it is not, the point is generic and the answer is yes with probability λ. Two independent Q per candidate and the summands fall out of 2|F| whole-base queries, with no sub-base query anywhere. The group operations that build them cost k · 22l against the m · 22l the linear algebra already pays, so they are absorbed.

    Measured at n = 13, 17, 19 over eight rungs, 64 built targets each, zero sub-base queries on every one. The two ways it misfires are collisions of Q with a summand or its negative — a miss at rate Θ(m/|F|) per draw, a false positive at Θ(m/|F|) + λ — and the measured rates stay inside 0.22–0.87 of those predictions across a sixteenfold range of m/|F| and of λ, with no third error term. Read off at the free-oracle optimum for m = 4 (l = 26.70, m/|F| = 2−24.70): localisation fails on one target in 220.66, losing 26.04 of the 226.70 relations needed.

    So there is one free-oracle floor, not two: 256.76 at m = 4, under the 260.81 reference from m = 4 onward, monotonically, with no table. The only detector this fails against is one restricted to a fixed family of targets that refuses R − P + Q — it would have to extract witnesses by meet-in-the-middle, bottoming at 256.93 with a 253.82-entry table — and no proposed detector has that shape: a resultant-vanishing test, a trace condition, a fixed-degree Gröbner refutation and the Nagao/Riemann–Roch coefficient search are all algorithms on the target's coordinates. Two earlier revisions of this panel priced that distinction as the curve's protective margin, first at 237.68 and then at 211–224. The margin is not there; class accounting both times (experiments/ecc2k130_point_decomposition.json, experiments/ecc2k130_decomposition_targets.json).

    The six pre-registered experiments have been run, and no falsifier fired. The product law is now evidence at n = 13 and n = 19 rather than arithmetic: every end-to-end rung recovered its planted logarithm, every relation was re-added in the group before entering the matrix, and the slope of log₂(total) against n is 1.037 0.944 ± 0.028 → 0.976 ± 0.024 against a falsifier of 0.95. The first struck figure is the superseded full-rank stopping rule; the second is the relation budget on two rungs, which read below the falsifier. Fitted on three — n = 13, 19, 23, mean Λ 3.489, 2.766, 3.020 — the slope is 1.1 standard errors above it instead. The third rung reversed the sign: n = 19 sits 0.138 under the fitted line and was dragging a two-point join down with it, where a two-point join has no residual in which that could show. The two error estimates now agree (0.0241 from seed noise, 0.0239 from scatter about the line), a check the two-point fit could not perform.

    There is no fourth rung, and that is a fact about the curve family. This panel previously said n ≥ 29 needed field tables that do not fit in memory. They are not rungs at all: a rung needs a prime subgroup that is nearly the whole curve, or n does not mean what this axis says, and at n = 29 the largest prime factor of #E is 16,067 against a cofactor of 33,412 — a 214 logarithm wearing a 229 label. n = 37's cofactor is 596. Censused over 11 ≤ n ≤ 61, exactly four degrees have the ECC2K-130 shape — 13, 19, 23 and 41, every one with cofactor 4 — and n = 41 costs 6.6 × 1012 oracle operations. E1's four-rung falsifier cannot be fired on this family at any size this repository can run. n = 11 is separately excluded because its 23-torsion has rank two, so no cyclic subgroup of order p exists to pose the logarithm in. Class accounting.

    Sweeping the factor-base dimension at n = 19 moves the yield λ by a factor of 6,600 and moves Λ = ops/2n by 2.4: the dimension is measured not to be a lever, which is the whole content of the product law. The model's predicted rise above the saturating dimension does not occur — it is an artefact of charging one relation per target — so the model is conservative there, not wrong. The Frobenius orbit collapse delivers exactly n (13.0/13, 19.0/19) with relations that reach full rank and solve, which confirms the unchecked half of the seven-bit correction above. And the yield is Poisson to 0.90–1.10 across eight cells counted exhaustively over the whole odd subgroup, once the subsets containing a point and its negative are removed; those degeneracies, not the tail, are the entire source of the raw 1.44–2.98 over-dispersion.

    The other constant is withdrawn too, and it was the same error. This panel previously read “large-prime pairing produces relations that are 5–11× redundant”. That statistic divided the rank by however many paired relations the run collected, which is a harness choice and not a cost. Its own rows say so: two cells share a factor base (n = 19, l = 7, |F| = 139) and differ only in l′; the second collects 2.2× the relations, moves the rank by exactly one (134 → 135) and halves the ratio. On a small base run long it reads 0.0069, which by the same convention is “145× redundant”. Measured at the rank ceiling instead, the cost is 3×: rank/relations spans 2.0× across five cells against 52× for the published version. And the mechanism is the one retracted above — paired relations at m = 2 are differences, so they are edges of a graph on the base and reaching the ceiling is graph connectivity, about (|F|/2) ln|F| edges, making rank/relations ≈ 2/ln|F|. Measured against that prediction: 0.73, 0.87, 0.68, 1.01, 0.88. Both constants this thread called optimistic were the coupon collector in disguise. What survives is structural, not a constant: differences cap the rank at |F| − 1, so a large-prime pipeline at m = 2 cannot pin absolute logarithms on its own. Exponents untouched, verdict at n = 131 untouched; class accounting (experiments/ecc2k130_decomposition_runs.json).

    The second one is withdrawn. This panel previously read “reaching full rank took 2.0× the |F| relations the law budgets at n = 19, because decompositions harvested from one target are correlated.” Both halves fail. The excess is the coupon collector: a harness that stops only at full rank over every column spends |F| ln|F|/m relations, so the ratio is ln|F|/m and grows with the base — predicted 1.391 → 2.089 across the sweep against measured 1.453 → 2.395, never a constant. It is not target correlation either: first_hit shares no target between relations and shows the same excess, higher at two factor-base sizes and lower at two. And a descent does not need full rank — at the |F| relations the law budgets, every descent landed in 1–3 attempts, each landing checked against its planted logarithm, and Λ = 3.103 against the predicted m = 3, where the superseded full-rank rule read 5.136 and 5.993. The 2124.99 headline is unchanged: cost_cell always priced ρ = 1, so this removes a caveat rather than buying a bit. Class accounting (experiments/ecc2k130_decomposition_runs.json → relation_budget_and_stopping_rule).

    E2's l = 5 outlier was blamed on the same thing and is also something else. That cell ran 15,455 targets and stalled at rank 28/29. Enumerated exhaustively over every one of the 810 decompositions the base admits, the row space has a rank ceiling of 28 that no relation count can pass: every reachable triple there uses exactly one even-abscissa point, so the vector +1 on odd abscissae and −2 on even ones annihilates every row. From l = 6 the base admits all-even triples and the rank is full. Class accounting.

    E3's deferred item is now run on the pair it asks about, as a stage diagnostic. Section 3.2's swap localisation queries detector(R − P + Q), which is only sound if a detector charges the same for that as for R. ic swap builds R as an m-sum of base points, forms R − P + Q for a summand P and a class-matched Q, and hands both points of each of 64 pairs to every oracle: at degree 13, m = 3, matrix-F4's ratio cost(swap)/cost(R) is 0.502–1.363 with median 1.000, dearer in exactly 32 of 64 pairs, and its worst swapped pair sits below the worst pair of unrelated targets (1.814); SAT's median is 0.968 with the heavy tail of a randomised search on both sides (31/33). No oracle is systematically dearer on the swap. This panel's earlier “groebner flat to 6.3% across seven targets” is withdrawn: it swept ic run --known-log, never built a swapped point, and averaged away a 2.4× per-call spread; class accounting. Two toy rungs, one base each, one seed: nothing is inferred about a full ECDLP and no speedup is claimed (experiments/ecc2k130_e3_solver_panel.json).

    What would count next

    The candidate this panel named has been measured. Decomposing into two base points instead of three does carry orders of magnitude: the per-residual constant falls 580×, from 0.9 million field multiplications to 1,513. It also lands far above rho, at 1,037× at 33 bits, so by this ledger's own test the fixed-degree direction is quantitatively closed at toy scale.

    What is left is not a cheaper oracle. Two routes were measured and both are shut: a Gröbner solve on the descended system for fixed X₁ has a deciding degree that grows as ℓ/2, and the multilinear block structure of these systems cannot be used as a Macaulay shift restriction at all, because the only shift that preserves multilinearity is the trivial one. The open direction is a border basis in place of the fixed-degree Macaulay cut, and a merge-level cap for the large-prime linear algebra. Both were built or bounded, and neither helps. The merge-level cap is measured in §11.11: it lowers the solve exponent 0.045 ± 0.017 and the eliminator cancels it, leaving the method +0.051 ± 0.031 worse end to end. The border basis was bounded in §11.13 at 1.06× and then written (§11.14), which showed the bound charged work to the wrong rows. The normal forms read 149 of the 222 pivot rows, but those were reduced through almost all the rest: the rows they depend on are 202 of 222 at every size, the work outside them is 1.1% of the elimination, 0.19% of C₃ (5.6% as §11.13 counted it), and the ceiling is 1.002× (accounting). The solver gets 98.9% of that on the residuals it solves; the 0.3–2.4% whose staircase differs from the per-curve plan cost it a wasted attempt, so it loses 0.08–0.14% at p = 271 and gains up to 0.14% by p = 2083 — 1.0009× pooled end to end, zero mismatches over 20,146 cross-checked residuals. It stays off by default. What §11.5 already does — forward elimination plus memoised back-substitution restricted to the monomials actually reached — is a border-basis computation in all but name, which is why nothing was left. Class engineering for both, and neither is a finding.

    What would count now is a change in the closing rate, not in a constant (§11.15). At k = 3 every constant lever is spent, and the obstacle is structural: the linear algebra over |F| ∝ n1/3 unknowns costs n2/3, above rho's n1/2, and the large-prime cure closes only as n−1/18. The one lever left is the extension degree. At k = 4 the linear algebra is |F|2 ∝ n1/2, the same exponent as rho, and the relation phase grows as n1/4·C₄, so the plain method's ratio to rho tends to a constant instead of growing. That constant is the sparse solver's cost against rho's and does not depend on the solve; C₄, the cost of one S₅ solve over Fp⁴, sets only where the relation phase stops dominating.

    Derived before building (§11.16, from §11.7's measured Wiedemann constant and Fp⁴ operation counts): the constant is 0.34–0.63× rho, so a plain k = 4 method would eventually beat rho by 1.6–3× and no more (measured below). This note's own solver bounds C₄ ≥ 7.1·1010 from the characteristic polynomial of a 4,096-dimensional multiplication matrix alone, which put the handover at n ≈ 2133–2137, extrapolated on the exponents n1/4 and n1/2, and a measured C₄ in this design could only move it later. Decomposing into three points instead (Joux–Vitse) sits near 36× rho at every size — measured at 6,945× rho, flat from 232 to 240 (the rho-parity ledger below): one three-point test costs C′ = 1.6·105 multiplications, not the 1,513 borrowed from the k = 3 pair test.

    Then measured (§11.17, four residuals at p = 269, each solve cross-checked against a meet-in-the-middle oracle, the constructed one returning its planted decomposition): the S₅ system has the predicted dimension 4,096, an Fp⁴ addition costs the derived 97 multiplications, and C₄ = 1.21·1012, 17× the floor. The same solver on generic systems of the same degrees predicts it within 4%, so the summation polynomial is no cheaper than any four octics. The handover moves to n ≈ 2149–2153 (extrapolated over the derived constant; narrowed below), with the relation phase at 4.3·108× rho at 32 bits — still about eighty doublings before the k = 3 crossover. A stage diagnostic: no end-to-end S exists for the full four-point method, and none is claimed; the three-point variant's end-to-end S is 8,126 at 240.1 (6,945× rho, the ledger below).

    Then the constant, measured (§11.19, registered in §11.18: eight prime-order curves over Fp⁴ at p = 269–1033, n ≈ 232–240, relations from a meet-in-the-middle oracle, the linear algebra run to a verified logarithm on every curve, rho run 16 times on each, all 128 verified): the linear algebra costs r∞ = 0.518 ± 0.031× rho, flat in n (fitted exponent −0.021 ± 0.017), inside the derived band. So a plain k = 4 method would beat rho by 1.9× and no more. The one derived input that was off was the filtering fraction, 0.897 measured against the 0.73 borrowed from k = 3, and at the measured value the derived formula gives 0.510. The handover narrows to n ≈ 2151.1 (2150.8–2151.5), extrapolated on the same exponents and C₄. Class: a stage diagnostic. It prices the linear algebra against rho, while the stand-in relation phase at these sizes is 1,054–4,988× rho and the S₅ one 4.3·108×. The registered outcome was confirmed.

    Nothing here threatens a deployed curve, and nothing is claimed to. The point is to locate the crossovers by measurement rather than extrapolation.

    ECC2K-130 Route 3: the symmetrised oracle closes at the gate

    Closes the gate because the symmetrised oracle costs 3.1 to 14.7x the enumeration it would replace on every rung, so no end-to-end build follows, a stage diagnostic.

    Class accounting for the structural finding, engineering for the oracle ratio, and the gate itself is a stage diagnostic. X4 asked whether the 2-torsion frame’s symmetrised oracle, measured at 350× the chained x-system, is an advance end to end. It could not run as registered. Its floor, Λ = m/n, needs a Frobenius-stable V ∋ 1. On E1’s ladder, and at ECC2K-130’s n = 131 where 2 is primitive, the only such V are F2 and the field, and the symmetrised base over F2 is the single point T. So both frames must use a non-invariant V, both sit on Λ = m, and the question is cost per relation. X4′ registered that as a gate before any run. The end-to-end build happens only if the symmetrised oracle is cheaper per relation than the enumeration it would replace. Frozen source: experiments/26_koblitz_symmetrised_gate.json; rules in research/notes/ecc2k130/RESEARCH_ECC2K130_ROUTE_TARGETS.md §X4′.

Group-addition equivalents per relation found, with word XORs priced at the raw rate, so every oracle cost is a lower bound. The reference is the cheaper enumeration rule on the same base. Zero gate failures on 128 calls.

    The gate is closed. Per relation, the symmetrised oracle costs 3.1–14.7× the enumeration it would replace on every rung, priced from below. The fitted slope in n is −0.029 ± 0.167, so the ratio is not falling, and the frozen calibration gives the same verdict. Wiring the oracle into collection would raise Λ, so the end-to-end build is not done. The thinnest margin is at n = 23: the ratio stays above 1 for any word-XOR price over 0.00072 GAE, and the ledger’s degree-23 entry gives 1.66. The 350× question is engineering by the registered slope rule, +0.18 ± 0.32 over three unbounded rungs, which is weakly determined. At n = 23 the symmetrised system is the better algebraic oracle, but both lose to enumeration. Nothing here bears on ECC2K-130’s security.

    With Route 3 closed, the ECC2K-130 routes thread has met its own finishing condition. Its ledger is the close-out at the end of research/notes/ecc2k130/RESEARCH_ECC2K130_ROUTE_TARGETS.md. No oracle built there beats enumeration per relation at any size measured. The m = 4 fall degree has since been measured (the panel below). The items still open (Crossbred’s α over four rungs and Crossbred on the symmetrised system, and a second literature pass) are left open by choice, with the reasons given there. Class accounting.

    The second literature pass has since run (X6′, 2026-09-24). Nothing reopens Route 5. Outside the survey’s exclusion set, no source gives an operation count at prime n with q = 2. GGMP’s three Frobenius-invariant constructions do not exist at q = 2, n = 131: ord131(2) = 130, Couveignes–Lercier with a torus needs n | 3, and with an elliptic curve it needs a multiple of n below 6. The “Koblitz structure beyond Frobenius” item is empty by structure: End(E) = Z[τ] is the maximal order of Q(√−7), with class number 1 and automorphisms ±1. The pass also found that X5′’s explanation was Kosters–Yeo’s, and that is recorded in the panel below. Class accounting.

    ECC2K-130 Route 4: the x-chain’s “fall at 3” is one hidden linear equation, Kosters–Yeo’s trace equation (2015), which the symmetrised chain does not have

    Shows the symmetrised chain falls at degree 4 on every rung while the x-chain falls at 3, a structural finding explained by one hidden linear equation and bearing nothing on cost.

    A structural measurement: no cost moves, so no S and none of the four classes. H1 of the Koblitz scaling target says every chained decomposition system has its first fall at exactly degree 3. X5′ tested it on the one chained family H1 had not measured: the symmetrised S3, chained at m = 4 through two intermediate points. That system has Boolean degree 3, like the x-chained systems. It was registered before any code for it existed. Frozen: experiments/27_koblitz_x5_fall.json, with an unregistered supplement that only raises the Macaulay size caps in experiments/27_koblitz_x5_fall_raised_caps.json.

Under the degree-fall definition that Kosters–Yeo and HKY use, the same event is recorded at 2, one degree earlier. “Censored” means the degree-4 matrix exceeded the registered default caps; the supplement removes that.

    By H1’s letter, H1 is falsified for the symmetrised chain. It falls at 4 on every rung measured, 96 draws, where the x-chain falls at 3, and the offset is flat in n. A diagnostic then explains the one degree, and the explanation was already published. It is Kosters–Yeo’s trace equation (arXiv 1503.08001, Prop. 4.9 and Cor. 4.11; HKY, CRYPTO 2015, Prop. 5). Both papers apply it to chained S3 systems of this kind (KY derive a fall at 2; HKY report “usually 2”), and the paper was already in this thread’s literature survey. X6′ checks the identification on 96 of 96 draws, and a wrong-functional control matches on none (experiments/28_koblitz_x5_trace_identity.log). That re-attribution is accounting. With x(R) known, the x-chain’s last link is t² + xRt + …, and t ↦ t² + xRt has a one-dimensional kernel, so one combination of its n quadratic equations is linear. The measured quadratic-part rank is n − 1 on every draw. That linear equation’s Boolean identity is the single rank loss H1 records at 3. It also holds on every chained row of H1’s own table that was checked (all but n = 7), and that table now carries an accounting caveat. The symmetrised last link has full rank n, so it has no such equation and shows no rank loss below degree 4, where trivial syzygies force one. That part, and the removal of the trace equation by symmetrising under T, is not in the ten sources X6′ read. It is recorded as absent from those sources, not as new. So the symmetrised system is not shown to be harder. What the diagnostic shows is that the x-chain gets one free linear equation and the symmetrisation removes it (experiments/27_koblitz_x5_syzygy.log). The one registered solve (icv1-f2m11-t67-05f5aa36) agrees with 4-sum enumeration on all 16 targets. Nothing here bears on ECC2K-130’s cost.

    X5″ (2026-09-24, registered before its code): the degree-4 kernel split, per arm, over 8, 8 and 2 draws at n = 9, 11, 13. “Literature” is the degree-fall definition (graded top parts, trivial syzygies removed). “Trivial” is the degree-4 span of the Koszul and field syzygies, which is n + C(n,2) in every row. “Identities” are the Boolean identities of linear falls below degree 4. Frozen: experiments/29_koblitz_x5_syzygy_split.json.

    X5″: the symmetrised chain falls genuinely at 3, one degree above the x-chain in both conventions. By the literature’s definition its first fall is at 3 on every draw, with exactly 2n falls, all to quadratics. The count is derived: its last link’s top part wR·wQ2·w4 stays bilinear when multiplied by either symmetric coordinate wQ2 = AS(U2) or w4 (by U or by W, corrected in X5‴), because squaring is F2-linear. The x-chain falls at 2 by the same definition. So X5′’s 4-against-3 is the literature’s 3-against-2, and the symmetrised system is not shown to be harder. In H1’s convention its rank loss at 4 is n + C(n,2) trivial syzygies plus 26–56 that are not trivial and not identities of linear falls (there are none). What those are is left open. An unregistered localisation puts all of it, in both arms and both conventions, in the single link whose x(R) is known: the two cubic links show no kernel and no fall through degree 4. A first run that under-counted the x-chain’s identities is kept and disclosed (experiments/29_prefix/); the symmetrised rows are unchanged by the fix. A structural measurement: no cost moves.

    X5‴ (2026-09-24, registered before its code): the residual is not the pointwise trace, and it stays open. For each value σ of its small block, the symmetrised last link is an F2-linear system in the chain unknown, a(U2 + U) + U2 + d. Its cokernel is killed by ψσ(z) = Tr(z(1 + a)/a2): Kosters–Yeo’s trace, but with coefficients that depend on σ. That structure is confirmed on every draw. The registered hypothesis, that the residual syzygies are pointwise multiples of ψσ, is falsified: no such syzygy exists at degree 4 on any of 18 draws, in either arm. The residual needs multipliers that mix the chain unknown with the small block (either alone gives 0). An unregistered regularity at ℓ = 4 (residual = a per-rung constant + the number of small-block points where the local system is consistent, on all 16 draws) breaks at ℓ = 5, and is recorded only as an observation. At ℓ = 5 a different regularity holds, and it survived an unregistered supplement whose prediction was stated before it ran (n = 15, 8 of 8 draws): the residual is exactly 2n. It splits as n syzygies realisable with multipliers of U-degree ≤ 1, plus n with small-block degree ≤ 1, and none with only bidegree-(1,1) multipliers. The link is an affine bilinear system in (U, σ). The theory it now has to be checked against is Faugère–Safey El Din–Spaenlehauer’s Jacobian-kernel description of bilinear syzygies (JSC 2011), which is not claimed to explain it here. The x-arm failed one registered gate, and the cause is identified and checked: X5″’s last-link matrix used the whole chain’s variables as multipliers. Frozen: experiments/30_koblitz_x5_residual.json. No cost moves, and no further run is proposed.

    The verdict does not depend on the degree. At m = 3 the route is above rho even with a free oracle. At m = 4 the lowest Macaulay degree there is, 2, already spends the whole margin the free oracle had; that is the 25.71-per-target budget of §5.3, seen from the oracle's side. What the degree decides is whether the route has an asymptote. At a constant degree the oracle is polynomial in the unknowns, which is the regime of the published sub-exponential estimates. The measured degree is not constant: it rises 5, 6, 6–7, 7 over ℓ = 2–5, and it rises at fixed surplus in all four registered ladder pairs, while the first fall degree stays at 3. In all 14 exactly measured cells it lies within one degree of the semi-regular reference, equal in 10 (it predicted the 7 at (10,5) before the run), which grows about linearly in the unknowns. Under that reference the m = 3 price at n = 131 is 2196.95, which is worse than an exhaustive search of the 2129 subgroup. That rests on the agreement seen at n ≤ 15 persisting to about 209 unknowns, and it is not measured. The discriminating next cell is (15,5), where the reference says 8; its degree-7 matrix needs a larger machine.

    m = 4, measured (2026-10-06). The decomposition size whose free-oracle floor is below rho refutes at ℓ + 4 for ℓ ≤ 2 (one degree above m = 3 at the same ℓ) and at ≥7 for ℓ = 3, as pre-registered. Like m = 3 it is flat in n at fixed ℓ, so the degree is set by m and ℓ, and the semi-regular reference, within one everywhere, overstates its growth in n. Any degree that rises with ℓ collapses the route: under either measured fit the optimum is the smallest factor base, where the route is a target search costing 2158.96 (m = 3) or 2173.13 (m = 4), above an exhaustive search of the subgroup; below the searched range (ℓ < 4) they price 2158.12–2170.90 with target counts past the 2129 subgroup, still above that search. Those are extrapolations of three-rung fits, marked as such; the verdict against rho is unchanged.

It was saturation: 5,248 points is above n = 41’s scarcity limit of 4,962, and the 13.1% recovery overhead inflated the compact scan. That is the third reading this round that saturation contaminated, after n = 31 and n = 59, so examples/koblitz_degree_census.rs now computes the width that keeps a degree measurable. icv1-f2m31-tm90707-c95f16f5 stays unpriced for the same reason it did last round, now with the number: |F| × C(|F|+1,2)/r puts 1,771 hits a target at r = 221, so its conversion measures recovery.

    Selecting a base was 5.6× its floor, and all of it was BigUints

    Engineering: keying the point index on the packed u64 cuts selection from 78.2 to 37.3 adds a point, with every counter identical and no advance against the floor.

    Class engineering. With collection's relation count at its counting floor, selecting the base became 23.4% of the pipeline at 78.2 group-addition equivalents a point. The algebra a point requires is 13.93: the half-trace lift that produces it, unconverted, plus the one Frobenius step that places it in its orbit. The rebuild was 89.7% of the call, and half of the whole call was stepping BigUint-backed points through a Frobenius the pair table has always done in one word. Keying the point index on the packed u64 and walking both orbit structures with the FastCurve takes selection to 37.3 adds a point, 2.7× its floor, and the whole pipeline to 1.17× single-target rho — 6.51× batch rho on the same 32 targets (§19). Frozen source: docs/ic/runs/koblitz-select-packed-20260922.json.

    The rungs were scanning the whole base

    Engineering: windowing the summand scan instead of scanning the whole base cuts end-to-end operations about 2.5x at equal relation yield, while the generic floor does not move.

    Class engineering. Collection is 97.8% of this pipeline and the ledger rungs scanned the entire factor base per probe. A full m = 3 scan meets each triple three times — once for each summand that can be the third — and keeps one sorted witness, discarding two; a window of w keeps all three chances at w/|F| of the scan. Priced end to end at equal relation yield, that is about 2.5× fewer operations on both rungs. The generic floor does not move — the window changes no count it bounds — and the contract's count floor, which is on attempts, gets worse: a window spends more trials per relation, not fewer. What falls is summand scans, which that floor does not bound. Frozen source: docs/ic/runs/koblitz-collection-window-20260921.json.

    Collection was waiting for rank, not coverage — and the relation count is now at its floor

    Advance: aiming the scan at least-mentioned columns reaches full rank at exactly 192 relations, the counting floor, with accounting corrections inside and S still 1.33x single-target rho.

    Class advance, with a relabelling and two accounting corrections inside it. Collection is 60% of this pipeline and its cost is proportional to relations banked, so why a run needs 333 relations for 192 columns decides what is left to win. Replaying a finished run answers it: coverage and full rank both complete at relation 330, the coupon-collector threshold C·ln(C)/3, because with three summands on uniform columns a column is missed with probability e−3R/C and the two thresholds coincide. Aiming the scan at uncovered columns moves coverage to 117 relations — a 2.8× move in the tracked number — and the total by 1.02×. Aiming it at the least-mentioned columns reaches full rank at exactly 192 relations, the counting floor: 192 unknowns need 192 independent equations, so no collection strategy can bank fewer and this lever is finished. S is still 1.33× single-target rho, which is 7.42× batch rho on the same 32 targets (§19). Frozen source: docs/ic/runs/koblitz-collection-aim-20260922.json.

    The probing volume is an input, and it moves every rung

    Engineering: passing the workflow's own probe volume to the tier choice moves all three rungs from compact to folded, with the floor ratio flat and no row an advance.

    Class engineering. The tier is a function of how much probing amortises the table build, and build_within cannot know that — it falls back on the volume its constants were calibrated at, 351,750,000 summand scans. The ic workflow knows its own exactly, and now passes it to build_within_for. Every ledger rung probes less than the calibration (1.45× to 1,266× less) and all three move from the compact tier to the folded one. Frozen source: docs/ic/runs/koblitz-probe-volume-20260921.json.

S is a lower bound: factor-base selection and the linear algebra are unpriced and left null, not zero.

    Hyperelliptic: one exponent survives the priced linear algebra

    Genus 4 retains an exponent advance, the genus 3 claim is withdrawn as accounting once the solve was priced, and the reduced factor base remedy does not pay.

    The one family in this ledger that measures below a real rho. With N the subgroup order and m ≈ p/2 the full degree-1 factor base, rho costs √N at any genus. The relation stage alone gives Sic/Srho ∝ g!·N1/g − 1/2, but the solve adds a second term, Ns/g − 1/2, where the solve grows as ms, measured s ≈ 1.4–1.7. Protocols registered before measuring, in research/notes/index-calculus/RESEARCH_HYPERELLIPTIC_IC_RHO.md.

    Genus exponent fit of Sic/Srho against log₂ N, rho’s walk renormalised to √(π/2), 95% interval. Factor-base walk, in-situ unit, round seven. Every run returned its verified k.
    grelation law two-term band measured best ratioClass
    20.000between 0 and +0.19+0.21 [0.00, 0.41] was −0.0270.29 was 0.94constant lead, rising
    3−0.167between −0.17 and +0.07−0.01 [−0.07, +0.05] was −0.1540.55 at N = 212.6 was 0.38accounting, claim withdrawn
    4−0.250between −0.25 and −0.09−0.29 [−0.42, −0.16] was −0.2750.24 at N = 224 was 0.21advance, exponent

    Round seven made the solve 5.1× cheaper and that is what withdrew genus 3. The sparse solve’s charge fell 2.0–18.2× (median 5.1×, A/A spread ≤ 1.4×; every candidate sweep beat every baseline sweep on all 18 rows) with relations, oracle counts and logarithms identical: engineering. The same measurement fixed the solve’s growth, and with it priced the genus-3 fit is flat: −1/6 lies outside its interval. The old −0.154 was fitted while the solve was charged almost nothing. This is structural: a full factor base makes elimination cost order p2 against rho’s p1.5 at genus 3, which is why the literature shrinks the factor base at small genus (Thériault 2003; Gaudry, Thomé, Thériault and Diem 2007).

    Round eight tested the textbook remedy and it does not pay here. A reduced factor base with single large primes (Thériault) was registered with per-row predictions and measured on 11 instances, including genus 2 up to p = 4001 where the model predicted a 4–6% saving. Measured: about 1% at best, nothing at genus 3 or 4 once seed variance is separated (a 0.864 at genus 3 p = 61 reads 1.003 at 60 seeds; the registered H1 and H2 are recorded as falsified). Combined rows are denser than the model assumed, and the charged partial bookkeeping costs 2–4%. Large primes do beat a reduced base without them by 1.6–3.8×. no change One new size: genus 3 at N = 3.2·107 reads 0.23 raw, 0.46 renormalised — a single row, not a refit. Frozen source: round eight.

    Superseded corrections, kept. Round five fitted against log₂ p and genus 4 missed at −1.611 against −1.0; restated against N, which the harness measures as p1.91, p3.20 and p5.94, it landed in band. Rho’s walk drifts to 1.71–2.10 on the largest rows against the ideal 1.2533, so ratios here renormalise it; the genus-4 best row reads 0.15 raw and 0.24 renormalised, and 0.24 is the number to quote. Round six then found the oracle under-charged 20–30× and the solve reported as rounding to zero; its in-situ unit is what these rows use.

    Scope: p ≤ 251, N ≤ 224, one x86-64 container, full degree-1 factor base, five sizes at genus 4 of which the four smaller lose. The O(p) factor-base build that dominates at cryptographic size is not modelled. Frozen sources: round seven (fits in fits.json, rows in fbwalk_rows.json); round five, superseded.

    ECC2K-130 Goal28: profiling and grid screen

    Engineering: the grid screen on a G7 RTX PRO 4500 found both smaller worker grids slower than the 385,024 control, no usable hardware counters were obtained and 28 B/s remains unmet.

    28 B/s remains unmet. These measurements use one G7 RTX PRO 4500; the historical 14.637530 B/s benchmark and 14.106673 B/s DP34 reference used an RTX PRO 6000. G7e capacity was unavailable. No cross-GPU speedup or full-DLP speedup is inferred.

    engineering The generic-group boundary remains Ω(√(n / 262)). Every screened variant still costs 5.3125 field products per scalar update, ratio 1.0 to control. The kernel experiment does not measure a new ECDLP exponent.

    WorkersBenchmark (B updates/s)Ratio to original gridDP34 (B updates/s)Ratio to original gridCorrectness / status
    385,024 control4.6494291.0000004.6022911.000000passed / screen
    192,5124.5341230.9752004.4833640.974159passed / slower
    96,2564.5372250.9758674.4730960.971928passed / slower

    Three repetitions per grid/workload, each completing 201,863,462,912 updates with zero drops. Distinct seed panels across grids make this a tuning screen. First rows are retained without a thermal-steady-state claim. Sorted DP multisets agree across repeats within each grid.

    Nsight Systems: four walk kernels totaled 628.592 ms; five kernel-launch API calls totaled 0.113 ms in the short diagnostic trace. Synchronization waits overlap GPU execution. Nsight Compute failed at kernel preparation in both full-set kernel replay and reduced-section application replay. No hardware-counter bottleneck is claimed; profiler durations are excluded from timings.

    A further independent CUDA smoke workload passed CPU comparison but failed profiler preparation in both kernel and application-range replay. After correcting a rejected CLI option, the ECC range command returned zero with “No ranges were profiled”; the missing-report gate rejected it. No usable hardware counters were obtained. Both attempts and two additional instrumented timelines are retained in the range diagnostic receipt.

    Raw runner failures remain recorded. An offline archive audit revalidated the completed screen after its postrun bookkeeping failure. Source: frozen measurement receipt; report and raw evidence. No default or production preset is promoted.

    Goal28: more resident warps did not improve throughput

    Engineering: MINBLOCKS=3 raised residency per SM without spills, yet all ten timing pairs favored the control and the 28 B/s goal remains unmet.

    engineering One G7 RTX PRO 4500, five alternating pairs per workload after four excluded warmups. Each sample completes 201,863,462,912 scalar updates. Field products stay at 5.3125/update, ratio 1.0; the generic-group boundary and exponent are unchanged.

    Launch boundBenchmark (B updates/s)RatioDP34 (B updates/s)RatioCorrectness / acceptance
    MINBLOCKS=2 control4.6920141.0000004.6326961.000000passed / control
    MINBLOCKS=34.5930110.9789004.5422810.980483passed / rejected

    Registers decreased from 104 to 80 without spills; CUDA confirmed residency rose from two to three blocks per SM. All ten timing pairs nevertheless favored the control. Cross-binary checkpoints matched, and every DP34 multiset contained the same 5,149 records with zero drops.

    Paired geometric speed ratios: 0.982453 benchmark, 0.980758 DP34. Exploratory 95% paired log-t intervals: [0.974553, 0.990417] and [0.973004, 0.988573], assuming independent approximately normal log ratios. The 28 B/s RTX PRO 6000 goal remains unmet; defaults remain unchanged.

    Source: frozen paired receipt; report and complete raw evidence.

    ECC2K-130 GPU engineering: per-SM oversubscribed waves

    Engineering: falsifies that more waves help the RTX PRO 6000, since oversubscribed waves never beat the 4-wave row per SM, so the campaign default stays four waves.

    engineering Same packed walk, 5.3125 field products per update, MINBLOCKS=2. Automatic occupancy is one wave; the 6000 shipping preset is four. 6× and 8× were unmeasured. Unit: M complete scalar updates per SM per second, so the 6000 integer-pipe remainder is a flat ≈85. One Modal allocation per SKU, one binary, waves 1/4/6/8, batch 16, 256-thread blocks, three complete-scalar repeats. Live 6000 searchers stay on 385,024 workers.

    GPU / wavesWorkersMedian B/sM it/s/SM/ 4-wave/ pipe ≈85ClassCorrectness

    “More waves help the 6000” is falsified: 6× and 8× are both ≤ 4× per-SM (0.995 and 0.994), and neither is >1% above the 4-wave row on that allocation. “The survey starved other SMs” is falsified on L40S: 4× is 0.897 of 1×. The 85 floor is a 6000 pipe remainder; L40S is not asked to cross it. Campaign default stays four waves on the 6000. Occupancy on that part is spent; remaining headroom is instruction cuts.

    Auxiliary inputs and torsion points against rho advance, DLPwAI only

    Finds Cheon rows advance only as DLPwAI against the floor their extra inputs allow, while standard-input rows do not move and the torsion-embedding route is closed by measurement.

    Frozen source: research/torsion_auxiliary_inputs_20260918/results/*.json, tables in its RESULTS.md; note research/notes/ecdlp-general/RESEARCH_TORSION_AUXILIARY_INPUTS.md. Unit S = ops / √p, affine additions, every phase charged, medians over three planted secrets, every row verified. Rows marked DLPwAI were handed [α^d]G (or [α^i]G, i ≤ 2d) by the problem and are scored against that problem's generic floor √(p/d); no row that sees only G and [α]G moved, as the Ω(√p) floor requires. The torsion-embedding route (an auxiliary curve's [d]-map in place of Fp*) is closed by measurement. No index-calculus row exists: the inputs' logarithms are polynomially related and the relation matrix is linear. Torsion points on the target curve enter index calculus only as symmetries (negation, 2-torsion translation, automorphisms, Frobenius); the counting floor κ ≥ √(2(B+1)/γ) falls with the automorphism order γ by the same factor the generic yield bound γP²/2n rises, so a symmetry is already priced into the boundary and quotienting by it leaves the ratio to the floor unchanged: engineering, never advance.

    p − 1 case, d ≈ p1/2, inputs G, [α]G, [αd]G. Fitted exponents over seven sizes (24–48 bits): rho 0.487, comb 0.231, naive 0.297, kangaroo 0.310.

    Torsion-symmetrised index calculus on Koblitz curves, end to end engineering at n = 17, 23; refuted at n = 31

    Finds the symmetrised arm cheaper per solve but decomposing fewer targets, engineering at small n, refuted where the u-base needed 2.6x the trials, with the rho gap growing to 63500x.

    Frozen source: research/koblitz_symmetrised_e2e_20260927/results/*.json (every ic bench report) and *.fb.json (every factor base point by point, with each point's u = 1/(x+1), column and BLAKE3 of the list); contract in its README.md, tables in RESULTS.md; note research/notes/index-calculus/RESEARCH_EXOTIC_COORDINATES.md §20. Unit S = GAE / √r over the whole pipeline (base, walk, every decomposition attempt, matrix, verification), mean of three planted logarithms, every run verified, eight counted rho runs per instance on the same seeds. The two algebraic arms are priced by measured wall at the host's ns/add (their word-XOR count covers the eliminations only), serially; S_xor in RESULTS.md is the counted floor. Both arms share the runner, the relation loop, the pricing rule and the rho column: sym is the base Fu = {P : 1/(x+1) ∈ V} closed under +T with the summation polynomial in w = u²+u, s = Σu; x is the plain x-frame base {P : x ∈ V} with the plain Weil descent, same V, same inherited-F4, Macaulay cap 3.

    m = 2, same V (dim 9 / 12 / 12 / 11), same seeds. The +T-closed base decomposes about 0.6× as many targets (representations come in pairs), the w, s solve is 1.5–2.4× cheaper per trial in measured wall; the net is the product.

    Crossbred as a decomposition oracle: fastest oracle, still loses the pipeline

    Finds Crossbred the fastest oracle yet the worst pipeline arm at larger m, relation rate 0.0006x enumeration, with no advance and the oracle-as-pipeline reading named relabelling.

    Joux–Vitse Crossbred wired into Koblitz index calculus as DecompositionStrategy::Crossbred (Route 1 of the ECC2K-130 routes note, whose metric and falsifier were declared before this run). Two phases, two units, because the oracle result and the pipeline result point opposite ways. Frozen source: oracle ladder, end-to-end panel. Write-up: research/notes/ecc2k130/RESEARCH_ECC2K130_CROSSBRED.md.

    Oracle phase. Unit: bit operations, one 64-bit word XOR = 64 bit ops. Boundary: exhaustive search over the Boolean system, 2v·T. The declared metric is the wall-clock xb/F4 ratio at m = 3; the falsifier was xb/F4 ≥ 1 and does not fire.

    No row is an advance. The floor is Θ(2n) relation collection with any oracle polynomial in the factor base, and every arm sits against it identically; a faster oracle buys reach, not an exponent. One structural finding carries the whole round: no (D, k) in the sweep produced a single filter, so on these systems Crossbred is Macaulay preprocessing in front of 2k linear solves, paid per target — which is what the decaying wall-clock margin measures.

    The Riemann–Roch encodings in front of WDSat: one engine win, one tool ceiling

    Finds WDSat with Gaussian elimination decides every RR norm instance with far fewer conflicts than plain WDSat, while RR incidence crashes before the solver, so the round is abandoned with no advance.

    WDSat is the Weil-descent SAT solver this repository vendors for the frozen S4 regression; the Riemann–Roch incidence and norm frontends had never been put in front of it. New ANF exporter (ecc2k130/codegen/wdsat.py) and matched suite. Frozen source: n = 9 panel, solver ceiling probe. Write-up: research/notes/ecc2k130/RESEARCH_ECC2K130_WDSAT.md. Not a run of the frozen S4 regression — a different encoding is a different instance family and, because WDSat's structures are statically allocated, a differently compiled binary, so AGENTS.md §8's equivalent-suite route applies.

    Eight targets per formulation at n = 9, ten-second budget, both arms on the identical equations. Unit: conflicts, each solver's own counter. A timeout is neither a model nor a refutation; a crash is neither, and is reported as neither.

    Weil-descent SAT on the ECC2K-130 curve: the cheap regime ends at d = 7

    Records a measured negative closure: conflicts jump by about 370x across one dimension where pairs grow 3.2x, and the SAT route on this descended system is closed.

    The successor to the two Riemann–Roch lines above, on the real curve. The Nagao norm encoding and Trimoska's S′4 are compiled to F2 in a polynomial basis with the factor base V = {deg x < d} — the layout that keeps S′4 to 9d − 3 variables — and given to CryptoMiniSat with native XOR clauses (conflicts recovered by bisection on confl_limit, so the reference arm finally has the declared unit) and to WDSat, against brute-force pair enumeration as the null object. Contract frozen with its prediction before the run. Frozen source: RESULTS.md, contract, raw (CryptoMiniSat), raw (WDSat). Write-up: research/notes/ecc2k130/RESEARCH_ECC2K130_RR_SOLVER_PANEL.md §11.

    K0 over GF(2131), four uniform and four planted targets per d, 300 s per solve. Unit: CryptoMiniSat conflicts to decide (mean of the four uniform exhaustions); WDSat decisions. Boundary: pair enumeration, C(A, 2) unordered abscissa pairs. Decompositions of uniform targets begin to exist at d = 45; every row measures exhaustion, never yield. S against the group order is uncalibrated: this prices an oracle, not an attack.

    Reading the d ≤ 6 one-conflict refutations as a fast oracle————relabelling — the certificate expires 39 dimensions before decompositions exist

    The contract's falsifier asked for a slope of log2(conflicts) below 1.8 per dimension over at least four complete sizes. Five exist (d = 4–8) and their least-squares slope is 4.62 with a residual standard error of 4.38 — two regimes joined at d = 7, not a power law: one dimension costs 370× in conflicts where it costs 3.2× in pairs, and the next is out of budget. The obstruction is the one §9 of the panel note measured — the S4 value-set span saturates F2131 at d = 7 — seen from the solver's side, and it closes the SAT route on this descended system and the coefficient encoding under SAT. It does not speak to an encoding whose value set stays proper at d = 45, or to a factor base that is not an F2-subspace. No row is an advance; nothing here is a statement about 2131.

    Where the tournament collector crosses rho engineering

    Measures the crossing between n23a1 and n37a0, ratios 0.831 and 1.396 against the worker rho, but an accounting note finds that rho unmatched, so no cell is shown below matched rho.

    Rounds 0019 and 0020 put this collector strictly below rho on an eight-cell Koblitz panel whose largest subgroup order is 4.2×106, and classified the gain engineering because the Θ(r2/3) against Θ(r1/2) shape was derived. The collector was capped at degree 31 only because its pair table packed coordinates into u32; widening that field to u64 opens n37a0 and n43a1, 55× and 1100× the panel's largest cell. These numbers supersede round 0021's, which charged rho on four fixtures where it had not finished and measured every cell at a factor base that is optimal only on the panel. 64 fixtures a configuration over two seed streams, both arms required to complete, every index-calculus report checked by the independent oracle.py certificate checker. No tournament ran and nothing was promoted — this is a measurement against the round-0020 winner source, with no stage summaries and no evidence pack.

    Evidence: full result · the ladder · factor-base sweep · what the trial cap is worth · the superseded round.

Given the IC arm’s own orbit naming, that rho beats the lane’s IC pipeline at every cell measured, by 1.19–2.88×.     The best base grows with r — 8, 16, 24 orbits across 1100× in r, about r0.157 — which is far slower than the F = (c·#E·t/k)1/3 the same model derives, and that model predicts 30 and 83 orbits at the two cells rather than 16 and 24. The two predictions are not independent: r1/6 is derived from the base sitting at that optimum. So the agreement on the rate, at a base measurably not where the derivation puts it, is a coincidence the model does not yet explain rather than a confirmation of it.

    The trial cap was raised from 4096 to 65,536 so rho finishes at every cell. That is a protocol change, not an extension — max_trials is rho's iterations-per-restart — but it is worth at most 14 ppm in instructions on either arm, both signs, and n23a1 reads 0.831 at both caps to three decimals. The rounds-0019/0020 strict win is untouched and stays scoped to its eight cells, its two seeds and its subgroup orders. Earlier calibrated rows, fitted exponents and the page's end-to-end verdict are unchanged.

    A triple-sum table moves the crossover engineering

    Finds the triple-sum table an engineering rate change, moving n37a0 to 0.813 of the worker rho and n43a1 to 0.933, but a correction says that rho is unmatched.

    The collector above is a pair table: Θ(r2/3) at its own optimum, a boundary its model scopes to “this pair-table collector, not index calculus”. Tabulating triple sums Co + Pj + Pl under the same Frobenius orbit names and scanning one summand per probe gives four-term relations and Θ(r3/5), so the ratio to rho grows as r1/10 rather than r1/6 — derived, not fitted. A patch against the scaled tree, on two orbits where the pair table uses 8, 16 and 24; pre-registered before it existed. Not a tournament round: no native-time gate, no confirmation or replay stage, nothing promoted.

    F5 for the Koblitz Gröbner stage: the criterion prunes nothing at degree 3; inheriting the parent’s reduced basis, splitting on the variable that displaces the fewest of its rows, and rewriting only the rows a level touches cuts the stage 21× engineering

    Two F5 ideas applied to the matrix-F4 splitting solver behind the Koblitz decomposition oracle. The F5 criterion, stated correctly for the Boolean ring (the textbook F_2 rule “prune t·f_i for t ∈ LM⟨f_1..f_i⟩” is unsound there, because x₁·(x₁x₂+x₁+x₂) = x₁; the Frobenius syzygies must enter as polynomials), removes nothing from the quadratic degree-3 matrices the oracle solves — the trivial syzygies live at degree 4 — and 0–12% of rows where linear equations appear: 1.001× net of its own cost. Inherited matrix-F4 applies F5’s idea to the axis the solver actually iterates along: substitution is a ring homomorphism, so a child’s Macaulay row space is the image of its parent’s reduced rows, and only the rows whose pivot contains the assigned variable need re-reducing. No matrix is built below the root. Two measured facts then set the constant. Which variable decides how many rows are displaced: a pivot is a row’s largest DegRevLex monomial, so the historical rule — split on the lowest-indexed free variable, the largest in the order — picks the variable most pivots contain and displaces half the basis per level deep in the tree; splitting on the smallest free variable halves the engine’s work and turns its one loss (the chained cubic systems, 0.60×) into a win. And three quarters of the rows a level keeps are never touched at that level, so a kept row is shared by reference and rewritten into a newer layout only when something needs it, through the composition of every step since, charged once.

    Boundary: the m·2131 candidate-tuple count of the ECC2K-130 decomposition note — no term for how a Macaulay matrix is reduced or how many are built, so the ratio to it is flat by construction. Reference: SolverEngine::MatrixF4 { max_degree: 3 } splitting on the lowest free variable, the pre-round default, on the same binary (KIC_F4_INHERIT=0). Unit: 64-bit word operations; the candidate is additionally charged one per word read and written every time a row is rewritten, which the reference’s matrix build never pays. Two comparisons are drawn and named: same-tree, accepted by the frozen suite’s compare.py (identical verdict digest and node counts), and cross-tree against the pre-round default, where the split rule changed the tree’s shape — same instances, same targets decomposed, no exhausted budget, every decomposition lifted and verified in the group (compare_cross_tree.py). Evidence: manifest · cross-tree ladder · same-tree ladder · same-tree, historical rule · holdout · F5 criterion · note.

    The chained Koblitz system: fix the last summand first, eliminate the intermediate point — 4.91× on a registered holdout, only together engineering

    Fixing the last summand first and eliminating the intermediate point gives 7.25x on the holdout only together, order alone 0.21x, with a flat floor ratio, classed engineering stage diagnostic.

    For m ≥ 3 the decomposition oracle solves the chain S₃(x₁,x₂,e₁), …, S₃(em−2,xm,xR), and the inherited engine’s split rule, handed the layout order, branches first on the n coordinates of the intermediate point — the least constrained unknowns in the system. The system is multilinear in its blocks, so once the ℓ coordinates of xm are fixed the last link is linear in em−2. Two changes act on that: the order (groebner_decompose renames the chain x₁, x₂, e₁, x₃, …, xm so the same rule fixes xm first, and renames each root back before lifting it), and linear elimination (a node’s degree-one generators are Gauss–Jordaned and substituted away — an affine substitution is a Boolean-ring endomorphism, so every root is kept — and the node rebuilds a small basis over what is left). They only work together: the order alone is 0.21× on the holdout, because the last link’s generators drop to degree one and the engine multiplies each by every monomial of degree ≤ 2; elimination alone is 2.42×; both are 7.25×. A third, same-tree change — rebuilding a child’s basis on any degree drop instead of completing it — failed its own registered gate (0.88× on one holdout rung) and stays a retained control.

    Boundary: the m·2131 candidate-tuple count of the ECC2K-130 decomposition note, no term for the split order or for how a node is reduced — the ratio to it is flat by construction. Reference: the shipped default on main (KIC_CHAIN_ORDER=layout KIC_LINEAR_ELIM=0), which reproduces main’s frozen ladder to the digit; unit: 64-bit word operations, with the elimination’s row operations and every monomial its substitution writes charged to the candidate. Registered, and the registration bit: the first holdout was written without an admissibility check, seven of its eleven cells never enter the Gröbner stage, and T1 needed six comparable rungs — T1 is not met as registered. The supplementary holdout T1′, every admissible cell of a screen that no arm had touched (nine), was registered before any run on it and met the same thresholds; so did the frozen-ladder no-regression target and the correctness target. Two of the exploration’s cells, including its largest ratio, turned out to be inadmissible and are not evidence. Evidence: all eight arms · T1′ · holdout · frozen ladder · admissibility screen · manifest · note.

    Support-local multipliers: build each root row from the generator’s own variables — 1.50× on a registered holdout in word operations, 1.12× in instructions engineering

    Support-local multipliers meet the registered 1.3x threshold in word operations but read only 1.12x in instructions, and a hashing regression fixed after registration shows relabelling risk, classed engineering.

    The inherited engine built a root’s Macaulay matrix, and every completion after a degree drop, by multiplying every generator by every monomial of the allowed degree over every variable occurring in the system. For the chained systems of the previous round that is mostly wasted: the links are block-multilinear, and a product of the last link with a variable of the first summand makes monomials that nothing the tail reads can use. Support-local multipliers multiply each generator only by monomials in its own variables. That is a subset of the old rows, so every consequence is still in the ideal and no root is lost; the tail can only be weaker, so the tree can only grow (it grows by at most ten nodes on any rung). Quadratic m = 2 roots already span every variable and are built identically.

    Boundary: the m·2131 candidate-tuple count, with no term for which rows a root is built from — flat by construction. Reference: the previous round’s default on main, selected on the same binary with KIC_F4_MULTIPLIERS=occurring, which reproduces that round’s frozen runs to the digit. Unit: 64-bit word operations; building a row is uncharged in both arms, as it always was. Registered before any run: a new holdout of 19 rungs (four cells no ladder had used, including icv1-f2m31-tm90707-c95f16f5 at 46 unknowns, and fresh targets on the fifteen known admissible cells), a 1.3× threshold with no rung allowed to rise more than 2%, the frozen ladder, and identical oracle verdicts. All three targets are met in word operations, the unit they were registered in. Re-priced in instructions (the accounting round), T1 reads 1.12×, below its 1.3× threshold, and 1.01× on the three icv1-f2m31-tm90707-c95f16f5 cells: most of the gain was in elimination, which the unit over-weights.

    What the unit missed. On the registered code the whole logarithms did 2.19× less oracle work and ran 18% slower (0.82×, interleaved, 95% interval [0.80, 0.84]). A profile found that the new root builder packed rows through an FxHash index. On one word that hash is x·K, which keeps x’s trailing zeros, so the tail links’ monomials (the low-index variables absent) fell into a few buckets. Packing cost 151 M instructions against 39 M for the elimination it served. That is the relabelling pattern of AGENTS.md §3, seen in wall time because S is null here. A post-registration amendment gives pack_rows and the engine’s column index the splitmix hasher the cached layouts already used. Every counter of all 60 amendment ladder runs and every whole-log run is identical to the registered runs. After the fix the whole logarithms run 1.41× faster than the reference. Evidence: stage tables · R2 holdout · frozen ladder · admissibility screen · amendment identity check · whole logarithms · profiles · manifest · note.

    Retained control: KIC_F4_MULTIPLIERS=occurring. Tests pin that support-local rows are a subset of the occurring-variable rows (equal at m = 2) and that every policy keeps every root with either multiplier choice. Nothing here moves a first fall degree, a solving degree, a fitted exponent or the page’s verdict: at n = 15, m = 3 the Gröbner oracle is still 3× enumeration and 60× meet in the middle per target. The lesson is for accounting: row building has never been charged, and this round shows an uncharged phase can grow and hide a regression. Pricing it is the next round’s first, registered, change.

    Follow-up, same day: environment lookups moved out of the per-row and per-node loops (a profile found 1.4% of a chained cell’s instructions in getenv). Every counter of 30 ladder runs and 120 whole logarithms is identical; the ladders run 1.03–1.07× faster in wall time and the whole logarithms are flat — engineering on uncounted work, no claim in the unit (evidence).

    The Gröbner stage priced in instructions: the word-operation unit sees 0.2–2% of it, and the whole logarithm is 964× rho accounting

    Pricing the decomposition oracle stage in instructions shows the word-operation unit counted a tiny share of it, and the whole logarithm costs 964x rho, so prior round gains are reclassified accounting.

    The Gröbner-stage rounds priced the decomposition oracle in 64-bit word operations: elimination XORs, specialisation reads and writes, linear-elimination row operations. Everything else was uncharged in both arms — building the system, building rows, sorting, hashing, allocating, scanning for leading terms — and the round before showed an uncharged phase can grow and hide a regression. This round prices the stage in instructions retired (callgrind), inside groebner_decompose for the stage and over the whole ic run process for a logarithm. A measured instructions-per-addition on the rho reference’s own arithmetic (924 at n = 13, 680 at n = 9) converts them to GAE, and rho is run on the same seeds in the same unit. Its instruction-derived S agrees with its counted one within 3%, which checks the conversion.

    Three arms on one binary: before #690 (A0), after #690 (A1), after #712 (A2, the default). Registered with gates, not a speed target. G1 met: every counter of every rung equals its registered run, and so do the whole logarithms’ trials, relations and oracle word operations. G2 not met as registered: one rung’s instructions vary by up to 2.5×10−5 between runs against a 10−6 gate; the cause, found afterwards, is rayon’s scheduling (single-threaded, the rung repeats exactly), and no ratio on the page moves by it. G3 met: every logarithm and every rho run verified. Adopted for later rounds: stage instructions beside word operations, a stage gain must lower the instruction total on the registered holdout, no-regression clauses apply in both units, and whole-log claims are stated in S from process instructions. Evidence: every rung and every run · pre-registration sweep · G2 diagnostic · manifest · note.

    Reading: round 1’s stage gains survive the re-pricing, round 2’s mostly do not on the large cells, and in the whole logarithm it is round 2 that moves the total (1.41× at n = 13, against round 1’s 1.01×). The unit over-weights elimination: 51 instructions per counted operation where m4ri kernels dominate, 586 where system construction and root builds do. The oracle ledger’s matrix-F4 figures are word XORs converted to GAE, so they undercount the oracle by roughly that factor. Next levers, measured here and not claimed: specialisation on the large cells (51% of instructions, insert 29%); system construction on the small and quadratic ones (31–33%), which #697 — merged after these runs — now amortises with an in-process template memo, not yet re-priced; and a layout cache for support-local roots, which would remove round 2’s one per-rung regression. Every figure here is for the code before #697 (31bedbdf).

    Complete cold Ir is user-space guest instructions, not curve additions. The K-instruction collector floor is implementation-specific and inapplicable to rho. Engineering rows test implementation changes; accounting rows are references or compatibility controls. Per-target identities, exact admitted bases, phase ledgers, uncertainty, retained failures and the final gate are available in the linked frozen report.

    Generic/reference qualification: complete evidence, no promoted IC winner

    Run 36290704597 completed all 1,350 pairs with zero failures, the pairinv incumbent stays the cold leader, generic IC is far slower, and no IC winner is promoted, classed accounting.

    accounting Research note and archive · Frozen results · Registered protocol

    Measured development comparison; no promoted winner

    The registered run 36290704597 completed all 1,350 native/profile pairs (30 A/A, 330 smoke and 990 development), with zero research failures. The whole-mode observer study completed all 360 pairs, with zero incomplete or failed pairs. This is accounting and reference qualification on public synthetic toy groups. It consumes no improvement round and does not change the accepted reference binding. One of three improvement rounds is complete; two remain. No global optimum or held-out improvement is established.

    Decision and comparison scope

    The optimized pairinv incumbent remains the cold IC leader. Prepared both is the online point-estimate leader, at 0.9770794 times incumbent time, with a descriptive 95% interval [0.9176026, 1.043898]; this does not establish an IC improvement. Generic dense and sparse IC are roughly 3.7 times slower online, ten times slower in cold native time and 37 times more costly in cold instructions than the optimized incumbent. Future rounds must retain the optimized reference. Choosing the generic worker as a weaker baseline would not establish progress. The frozen selectors choose rho_incumbent_8 for cold instructions and rho_generic_dense_16 for online time. These are development selections; a reviewed, versioned binding is still required.

    Primary metric and uncertainty

    Every job solves one supplied public point. Native online time begins after reusable factor-base, index and log preparation, includes all target-dependent attempts, and ends after scalar replay. Fixture construction, launch and input loading remain outside this interval. Three process repetitions are medianed per point; equal-cell geometric means combine 15 development points across five cells. The repetitions are not 45 independent targets and this is not shared-target amortization. Intervals are descriptive paired development bootstraps, with the frozen estimator and seed; they do not correct for selecting leaders on this panel. IC/rho intervals resample their paired observations directly, rather than dividing marginal confidence endpoints.

    Supplementary complete cold accounting

    Cold native time is the full cold child process, including launch, input and reporting tail. It is not the primary single-target online metric. Cold Ir is Valgrind 3.22 amd64 user-space guest instructions with exclusive complete phase closure; it is not curve additions. S = Ir / sqrt(r) uses subgroup order r, not field size. The existing K-instruction floor applies only to these full-rank relation collectors and is not a universal IC bound; it is inapplicable to rho. No observer or witness overhead is subtracted.

    What the phase ledger supports

    Shares are means of per-run fractions of complete cold Ir, with equal target and cell weight. Generic precomputation accounts for about 77%; final relation LA accounts for less than 0.2%. The optimized incumbent spends about 1.6% in final relation LA. Eliminating that stage alone therefore cannot supply a 20% complete-cold improvement on these measurements. This is prioritization evidence, not attribution of cost to timers or witness generation. F4/F5 internal matrix reduction and final relation LA remain distinct stages.

    Whole-mode observer effects

    The registered enabled/legacy study checks semantic agreement and retains both outputs. It changes more than timers: collection mode, tracing and matrix/batch reporting also differ. Both modes retain witness reporting. Legacy has OBS1 observation identifiers and null scientific admission and phase costs. The common outer interval omits enabled phase-boundary bookkeeping, so it cannot replace the fully charged scientific online interval. Ratios near one do not establish zero or low timer overhead. No overhead is subtracted. The following 95% intervals are descriptive, from 10,000 paired within-cell resamples; they do not supply promotion evidence.

    Noise control and environment

    The 30-run A/A instruction gate passed. A/A online ratio is 0.9558727, interval [0.8785708, 1.005275]; cold process ratio is 0.9752561, interval [0.9240123, 1.025244]. This shows material wall-time noise. The experiment used the same Linux x86-64 Azure CI host, Rust 1.94.1, Valgrind 3.22.0, CPU affinity 3, one Rayon thread, 8 GiB and a 180-second child cap. The generic worker reported pclmulqdq dispatch. This is a virtualized CI environment; no bare-metal, ARM, GPU or FPGA result is implied. Host/runtime/build records are retained. The host manifest does not record the physical CPU model or concurrent host load; neither is inferred.

The dedicated Linux evidence CI must freshly restore the archive, reconstruct every export and pass all eleven frozen audits without worker execution.     PR #753 replayed all 8,192 toy policy-target outcomes, 2,137 target draws, four base constructions and all recovered scalars. Native-to-original cold field-multiplication components are 2.087–3.700 in the four held-out cells; native is cheaper than transported in two and dearer in two. Dual pullback and tagged source-orbit classification are charged. The conditional exact degree-263 smoke tested 32 public Certicom P,Q targets on each nonconjugate descending line [1,0] and [1,4] with 16 useful source/leaf points and one charged native leaf-orbit neighbor per selected point. All four 136-pair policies had 0/32 hits and rank 0 on both lines; 64 exact targets and 256 policy-target cases were independently replayed. Under uniform subgroup targets, the m=2 32-target union-bound expectation is at most 6.40e-36 hits per arm. Prior torsion discovery has a separate 3.267-second receipt without compatible field-operation metering, so no complete exact-target cost ratio is asserted. Scope and decision, toy cases, toy replay, exact smoke and exact replay preserve the evidence.

    Exact-target transport: PR #717 passed eight saved degree-263 representatives, 40 independent full-coordinate checks, 2,096 actual-degree kernel inputs, and 122 invalid-input controls. Its original validation did not include a reverse map. PR #750 verifies a normalized dual for all eight saved degree-263 maps; the all-line rational-kernel extension is recorded immediately below. Nonrational-kernel duals and exact-target PDP yield remain open. Compact producer: PR #720 promoted the n = 53 source and frozen 23,320-point base to main; its 12 archived witnesses were replayed in PR validation. The archived claim JSON still has its historical pending-validation label and does not by itself certify a main-based full-rank recovery. These are not cost rows in the toy table.

    All-line degree-263 transport: PR #1005 derives each kernel generator and complement from a frozen rational twist-torsion basis and verifies the normalized forward/dual identities on public P and Q for all 264 kernel directions, plus six fixed directions on a second independent basis. The producer and fresh-process replay agree on 141,480 nonzero forward/reverse twist-kernel exceptions, 540 off-curve kernel-abscissa rejections, 12 direct bit-polynomial full-coordinate reference lines, 20 other negative controls, and 264 distinct exact first-basis kernel sets. Both horizontal directions return to source b=1; the other 262 descend. All raw reverse maps compose as [-263] and the sign-corrected duals as [263]. The 598.296-second producer uses supplied torsion bases and is a correctness certificate, not a cold factor-base or PDP-cost row. Scoped decision and replay. A different leaf endomorphism order/discriminant does not by itself imply easier native PDP; natural n=131 yield, rank and full DLP cost remain unset.

    Native leaf representation: PR #973 passed the generic full-point addition edge on 20 small toy curves and both saved degree-263 leaves: 152,432 valid and invalid circuit evaluations, 19,974 archived rows, 40 actual-leaf controls, and zero reference mismatches (decision). PR #976 then bound three implicit native factor domains into a full-point chain. On GF(25), all 27 ordered triples and one wrong-target control per triple passed independent replay; the generic/generic SAT model lifted to the oracle point sum, and an unsupported toy target returned UNSAT with exhaustive oracle confirmation but no external proof trace. For the actual leaves [1,0] and [1,4], the complete chain used 1,312 primary inputs and 650,376/650,391 DAG nodes; exact target-O DIMACS size was 48,285,979/48,287,148 bytes (decision and replay scope). These are correctness and representation-size diagnostics, not PDP-yield or full-cost rows. The first two held attempts, with the initial narrow SAT witness and the second attempt's target-selector defect, remain archived.

    Native m3 counting admission: PR #991 used the balanced m10 screen's 79,770 total physical slot choices as a fixed budget. Even allocating them optimally across three ordered slots yields at most 18,799,877,179,000 tuples and a necessary one-coset target-support ceiling of 2.7624e-26; for one million uniformly marginal probes, the probability of any hit is at most 2.7624e-20. A 1% necessary ceiling instead requires at least 5,685,182,383,138 physical slot choices; retaining logs for all nonzero projected factors would leave at least 5,424,792,351 classes even after an optimistic free signed transported-Frobenius quotient. Exact bound and scoped decision. This rules out only the frozen m3 physical-budget/target-cap route, not larger bases or higher-arity solvers. No natural n = 131 factor count, PDP yield, rank or cost was measured.

Source low slots each have 7,977 physical points; fixed-leaf low slots vary from 8,063–8,339 and 8,087–8,323 respectively, so source one-slot Frobenius count transfer fails on each leaf. Balanced raw tuple products are 1.2789× and 1.3166× source, while uncompressed projected sign-class unions are only 1.02495× and 1.02793× source.     Equal-column m10 leaf bound: if a native policy only thins those measured collision-free, disjoint leaf slots to the source's cheap-Frobenius-normalized 3,988 balanced or 8,062 unequal log columns, the maximum ordered physical tuple counts divided by q are only 1.55032e−10 and 1.75611e−7. Even a counting ceiling of one requires at least 38,213 distinct leaf columns in this disjoint-slot model, 9.582× or 4.740× the two source budgets. This is a conditional no-go for that fixed-domain equal-column policy; redesigned overlapping slots or a verified cheap leaf action need separate support, solver, rank, and full-cost tests.     Public ECC2K-130 P and Q import directly into the rotated n = 131 model representation

    Verifies the public challenge P and Q pass on-curve, subgroup-order and Frobenius-scalar identities in both implementations, closing a representation prerequisite with no decomposition, log, rank or speed claim.

    PR #771 checks that the #762 polynomial z131+z13+z²+z+1 and bit-i coefficient encoding exactly match the repository's public challenge-point source. The literal P and Q each pass on-curve, subgroup-order and Frobenius-scalar identities in both the producer and an independent bit-serial/Fermat implementation; beta 3 has normal rank 131.     A replay of all five n41/L1,024 and n53/L1,024 block phase receipts found that index construction consumes median 35.27% and 28.40% of compact elapsed time. Under an explicitly conditional elapsed-share-to-CPU scenario, a per-instance selector that builds a second full index would need about 94% lower combined rank-and-target cost to reach matched-rho parity, even with free scoring; a zero-overhead single-index policy needs 37.86% and 53.85% lower rank-and-target cost. This is a planning threshold, not a measured selector or method no-go. The next trial is a target-blind, pre-index score with one selected index at n41/K255 on new Q, charged cold. Thus 0/6 cells are timing-eligible; no point-sum gain, rho crossover, no-go or ECC2K-130 transfer is promoted. The existing verdict and numeric reference rows above are unchanged. The diagnostic CPU table, seven raw artifact archives, failure and independent receipts are in the outcome report and PR #1079.
